Silver fell 3.52% to $55.94, platinum dropped 2.1% to $1,594.25, and palladium lost 2.6% to $1,059.05. The whole precious-metals complex moved lower together.

The argument of this forecast is that gold is not trading as a war hedge this week. It is trading as a rate asset, and the rates math has turned against it. A Houthi drone strike near Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah field pushed Brent to $111.99. Higher oil lifts inflation expectations, and that pushes Fed hike pricing higher. Rate futures now put a 90% probability on a December hike and 16% on a move at the October 27–28 meeting. "OANDA:XAUUSD" XAUUSD Early Friday, gold prices fluctuated around the 4,000 mark, closing at 3,997.8. Although technical indicators suggested a potential rebound, the price consistently failed to break higher—this "inability to rally" reflects the current market's underlying weakness. The downward adjustment is likely to persist when the market opens next week; the strategy remains to sell into strength (shorting under pressure). Any rebound should be viewed merely as a pause for the bears to regroup, rather than a signal of a trend reversal.While downward momentum has been somewhat depleted, the inertia of the existing trend should not be underestimated. At this juncture, the worst mistake is to subjectively guess where the bottom lies—the market will not grant you a reversal simply because it has "fallen enough." In the short term, watch for resistance at 4,055–4,060, with a key resistance zone at 4,085–4,090. Selling into rallies remains the prevailing approach.Technical StructureOn the 4-hour timeframe, as gold prices drift lower, short-term resistance sits at 4,055–4,060, with a major resistance zone at 4,085–4,090. The preferred approach is to enter short positions when the price encounters resistance during a rebound. On the downside, monitor the 3,975 level for initial support. Avoid chasing the market—do not short after a significant drop, and do not go long after a sharp rally. Good entry points are earned through patience, not by rushing into the market.Trading StrategyCore Approach: Prioritize selling into rallies; avoid chasing the market in either direction (do not short at lows, do not go long at highs).Short Strategy: Enter short positions in the 4,050–4,060 range; set a stop-loss at 4,073; target the 3,975–4,000 range. If the price breaks below this, hold the positions.Execution Guidelines:Wait for a rebound to the 4,050–4,060 zone before entering; do not jump the gun, and avoid shorting near the 4,000 level.Place the stop-loss above 4,073; do not hold losing positions indefinitely or use hedging (locking) strategies.Consider taking partial profits when the price reaches the first target zone of 3,975–4,000; if it breaks lower, look for further declines.If the price breaks decisively above 4,085–4,090, suspend short positions and move to the sidelines. ConclusionWe are currently in a phase where panic sentiment is battling against technical support. The lack of strength in any rebound indicates that the bears remain in control; however, as downward momentum exhausts itself, it is also unwise to aggressively chase short positions at these low levels. The core strategy is to "wait for a rebound, identify resistance, and then enter short positions"—discipline and patience are the true keys to long-term survival.If you found this analysis helpful, please show your support with a "like"! If you have a different perspective, feel free to share your thoughts in the comments. Follow the channel so you don’t miss any updates—see you during next week’s trading sessions!
